H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in Plessy v. Ferguson (ID: 163_0537-01) did not hold that mandatory racial segregation in railway passenger coaches violates the Fourteenth Amendment Equal Protection Clause. Instead, the Court held that the statute of Louisiana requiring railway companies to provide "equal, but separate, accommodations for the white and colored races" did not conflict with the provisions of the Thirteenth or Fourteenth Amendment to the Constitution. This decision effectively upheld the "separate but equal" doctrine, which was later overturned by the Court in Brown v. Board of Education (ID: 347_0483-01) in 1954.
